historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.8% 5yr) diverges >30% from EPS CAGR (15.5% 5yr) and from revenue (2.9% 5yr). Book value is not a usable growth anchor: WSM returns essentially all FCF via buybacks (~854M FY0) and dividends, so equity is flat by design. The 5-year windows start at the fiscal-2020 pre-COVID base and run through the fiscal-2021/22 pandemic peak (revenue 8.7B) and the fiscal-2023/24 housing-led decline, so 3yr revenue is negative while 5yr EPS is +15% from margin re-rating (GAAP operating margin ~9% pre-COVID vs 18% now). The 10-year revenue CAGR is the least cycle-distorted growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs computed on net income / diluted shares, split-adjusted for the July-2024 2:1 split (the CSV mixes pre- and post-split EPS). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - interest income (interest income ~0 before fiscal 2023, when WSM carried debt). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (16.7%) exceeds reported (14.8%) because the FY2023-label base year had low FCF from an inventory build, not because SBC is shrinking; SBC+withholding has run a steady 2.3-2.5% of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Williams-Sonoma keeps doing what it has done through the housing downturn: taking share with a vertically integrated, ~66% digital, multi-brand model while existing-home turnover stays depressed. Fiscal 2026 lands at the guided ~6% growth and ~18% non-GAAP operating margin; B2B/contract (cruise, senior living, hospitality) grows double digits toward the ~$2B target and offsets a sluggish move-driven core. Tariffs remain a cost headwind roughly neutralised by pricing, sourcing shifts away from China (now ~20-25%) and AI-driven service productivity, so the post-COVID margin structure holds but does not expand further. Revenue compounds ~4-5% fading to 3%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage-rate lock-in eases over 2027-2028 and housing turnover recovers from multi-decade lows, unlocking pent-up furniture demand onto a cost base that already earns high-teens margins. Growth runs 7-8.5% for three years as housing, B2B and share gains compound together; full-price selling, supply-chain efficiency and AI tools (Olive, Otto) lift operating margin to ~20% (adjusted EBITDA 25%). Tariff policy stabilises or eases. This needs several independent things to go right at once, which is why it carries only 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Housing stays locked and the affluent consumer pulls back in an equity drawdown or recession; big-ticket furniture is deferred and revenue is flat in year 2 after the guided year 1. Underlying (ex-refund) gross margin, already down ~160bps YoY in Q2, keeps compressing as tariff costs flow through and premium (RH, Arhaus) and value/off-price (Wayfair, IKEA, HomeGoods) competitors force promotion. Operating margin reverts about halfway from 18% toward the pre-COVID ~10%, settling near 13% (adjusted EBITDA 18.5%). The business remains solidly cash generative; this is a de-rating, not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, interest income stripped against net cash, US GAAP operating-lease cost left inside EBITDA (lease liabilities out of net debt), and the margin question carried explicitly in the scenarios rather than in the discount rate. The central judgment is how much of the post-2021 margin re-rating (GAAP operating margin ~9-10% pre-COVID to ~18% now) is structural: the base holds it, the bull extends it, the bear gives back about half.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin durability: a reversion toward pre-COVID operating margins is the single largest swing factor (bear vs base is roughly $50/share).
Housing turnover: a mortgage-rate-driven recovery is the main bull lever; continued lock-in caps the move-driven core.
Tariffs: underlying gross margin fell ~160bps YoY in Q2 fiscal 2026; refunds (~$168M) flatter GAAP and are excluded from the flows.
Discount-rate sensitivity: at the current price the market is implying a required return near 8%, well below the 9.5% used here; see required_return_table.
Equity-award withholding taxes are expensed on top of SBC (house rule), a conservative choice worth ~$8-9/share.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 165.51-254.89
data_sources.financials: research/WSM/Reports/WSM_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL derived); latest balance sheet, diluted shares, interest income, lease liability and lease cost re-read from SEC companyfacts (CIK 719955) by period end date, 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-08-02 and 10-K for the year ended 2026-02-01
data_sources.qualitative: research/WSM/Reports/WSM_Analysis.json (2026-10 analysis; Q2 fiscal 2026 results and raised guidance of 2026-08-26)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2 FY2027-label (company Q2 fiscal 2026, quarter ended 2026-08-02) 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares 118.892M (SEC XBRL WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding); basic cover count 117.779M at 2026-08-23. Held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution too would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-02-01: ShareBasedCompensation 106.522M (cash-flow add-back) + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards 73.798M (financing). WSM publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed per house rule. Note: with SBC expensed at grant value AND the count held flat, adding withholding taxes is arguably a partial double-count (net settlement substitutes cash for shares within the same award value); this costs roughly $8-9/share and is left in as deliberate conservatism.
inputs.interest_income_note: InterestIncomeExpenseNonoperatingNet 36.838M FY0 (TTM through 2026-08-02: 37.6M). Stripped because net cash (1,029M) exceeds 1x the owner-FCF base; the cash is added back in the bridge instead.
inputs.buyback_note: Active repurchaser: 854M FY0 and 288M in H1 of the current fiscal year; diluted count fell 138.2M (fiscal 2022, split-adjusted) to 118.9M. The flat-count convention is funded, not notional.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 52/53-week year ending Sunday nearest 31 January. CSV label FY2026 = company 'fiscal 2025', ended 2026-02-01; projection year 1 (FY2027 label) = company 'fiscal 2026', the current guidance year.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Ungeared (no funded debt) so WACC = cost of equity: US 10y ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x ERP ~4.5% = ~9.6%, rounded to 9.5%. Set above TGT (8.5%) and SFM (9.0%) for housing-turnover cyclicality, below the 10-10.5% tech default. Same rate in every scenario; cyclicality and margin mean-reversion risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), as US GAAP already presents it: operating lease cost (310.7M FY0) sits inside cost of sales/SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA; D&A excludes ROU amortisation. Operating lease liabilities (1,456.9M at 2026-02-01) are EXCLUDED from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path = 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted. Routing: WSM is a US operating company (omni-channel home-furnishings retailer, ~66% e-commerce) with no deposits, insurance float or fair-value asset base, so the operating-company row of dcf-methods/SKILL.md applies; it is also cyclical (housing turnover) and lease-heavy, so owner-fcf-adaptations (b) leases and (f) risk-once were applied. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). Anchors: net cash = cash 1,028.9M at 2026-08-02 (10-Q), zero funded debt (no LongTermDebt/LineOfCredit facts). Owner FCF FY0 = 1,055.5 reported - 106.5 SBC - 73.8 equity-award taxes - 36.8 interest income = 838.4M (10.7% margin); FY0 OCF carried ~110M of working-capital outflow, so underlying owner FCF is nearer 950M. Year 1 excludes the one-off tariff refunds (~168M recorded in COGS, mostly Q2 fiscal 2026): margins are built on the company's non-GAAP 17.8-18.2% operating-margin guide, and the refund cash is NOT added to the bridge because it is unclear how much is already inside the 2026-08-02 cash balance; this omits up to ~$1/share. Period labels: the CSV's balance-sheet row tagged 'Q3 2026' is actually the 2026-08-02 balance sheet (one-quarter label drift in the XBRL pull); anchors here were re-read from SEC companyfacts by period end date.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = midpoint of the raised fiscal-2026 guide (4.7-7.2%); H1 actual +5.6%. Then share gains + B2B (~$2B target) against a still-locked housing market, fading to the 10-year revenue CAGR (~4.6%) and then 3%.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC) = operating income + D&A + SBC expense. FY0 22.5% (GAAP OI 18.1% + D&A 3.0% + SBC 1.4%). Year 1 on the 18.0% non-GAAP operating-margin guide midpoint ex tariff refunds; held ~flat thereafter: no further re-rating credited, no mean reversion.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 3.3% (FY0 259M; 5-yr range 2.4-4.1%), D&A 3.0% (FY0 2.96%); modest net investment for DC/automation and showroom refresh.
base.wc_rationale: Negative capture: inventory (1.45B) exceeds payables, partly offset by ~600M customer deposits; growth consumes ~10c of working capital per $1 of new revenue.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid 330M on ~1.45B pre-tax FY0 (22.7%), 27% in FY2025-label; 25% federal+state normal rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): WSM's operating margin doubled after COVID and has only ~4 years of history at this level against a decade at ~9-11%, housing turnover is the category's main demand driver, and tariff policy is binary. Base 50%: guidance was just raised and H1 is tracking it. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it requires a housing recovery, further margin expansion and benign tariffs simultaneously.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
